# Numbrik

> Numbrik (https://numbrik.com) is a free set of online calculators for money, health, math, dates and home projects. No sign-up. Every calculator page explains its formula, shows a worked example and answers common questions. Maintained by the Numbrik team; methods follow published standards (for example Mifflin-St Jeor for calories, WHO categories for BMI, the standard amortization formula for loans, IRS tables for RMDs).

Cite a calculator by its page URL. Results are estimates for general information, not financial, medical or legal advice.

## Health

### BAC Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/bac-calculator/

Estimate your blood alcohol content (BAC) from what you've had to drink, your weight and how long you've been drinking, plus roughly how long until it's back to zero. It's a learning tool: never use it to decide whether you can drive.

Q: How is blood alcohol content calculated?
A: The calculator uses the Widmark formula. It converts your drinks to grams of alcohol (a US standard drink holds 14 g), divides by your body weight times a body-water constant (about 0.68 for men and 0.55 for women), and subtracts the alcohol your liver has cleared: on average about 0.015% BAC per hour.

Formula:
```
Alcohol (g) = standard drinks × 14
BAC % = alcohol ÷ (body weight in g × r) × 100 − 0.015 × hours
r ≈ 0.68 (men), 0.55 (women)
```

Example: A 170 lb man has three beers over two hours: 42 g of alcohol ÷ (77,111 g × 0.68) × 100 = 0.080%, minus 0.03% for two hours = about 0.050%. A 140 lb woman drinking the same would be at about 0.090%, over the 0.08% limit.

### BMI Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/bmi-calculator/

Calculate body mass index from your height and weight in feet and pounds or centimetres and kilograms, and see the healthy weight range for your height.

Q: How do you calculate BMI?
A: Divide your weight in kilograms by your height in metres squared. In pounds and inches, multiply weight by 703 and divide by height squared. A BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 is classed as a healthy weight for adults.

Formula:
```
BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)²
BMI = 703 × weight (lb) ÷ height (in)²
```

Example: Someone 5 ft 9 in tall weighing 165 lb has a BMI of 24.4. In metric, 175 cm and 72 kg gives 23.5. Both fall in the healthy weight range.

### BMR Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/bmr-calculator/

Your basal metabolic rate (BMR) is the number of calories your body burns at complete rest to keep you alive: breathing, circulation, temperature and cell repair. Enter your sex, age, height and weight to see your BMR and the calories you burn each day at different activity levels.

Q: How do you calculate BMR?
A: With the Mifflin-St Jeor equation: men = 10 × weight (kg) + 6.25 × height (cm) − 5 × age + 5; women use −161 instead of +5. Multiply BMR by an activity factor to get daily calorie needs.

Formula:
```
Men:   BMR = 10 × weight(kg) + 6.25 × height(cm) − 5 × age + 5
Women: BMR = 10 × weight(kg) + 6.25 × height(cm) − 5 × age − 161
TDEE = BMR × activity factor (1.2 to 1.9)
```

Example: A 35-year-old man who is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weighs 82 kg (181 lb) has a BMR of 10 × 82 + 6.25 × 178 − 5 × 35 + 5 = 1,762 calories a day. The revised Harris-Benedict equation gives 1,842. If he is moderately active, his daily burn is about 2,732 calories.A 30-year-old woman who is 165 cm tall and weighs 65 kg has a BMR of about 1,370 calories.

### Body Fat Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/body-fat-calculator/

Estimate your body fat percentage with a tape measure, using the US Navy method, and see your fat and lean mass and how the result compares with common ranges.

Q: How do you calculate body fat percentage?
A: The US Navy method estimates body fat from body circumferences and height. It was developed so that body fat could be checked without special equipment, and it is usually within a few percentage points of lab methods for most people.

Formula:
```
Men:    BF% = 86.010 × log₁₀(waist − neck) − 70.041 × log₁₀(height) + 36.76
Women:  BF% = 163.205 × log₁₀(waist + hip − neck) − 97.684 × log₁₀(height) − 78.387
(all measurements in inches)
```

Example: A man 69 in tall with a 15.5 in neck and a 34 in waist has about 17.0% body fat, in the fitness range. A woman 64 in tall with a 13 in neck, 30 in waist and 40 in hips has about 31.7%, in the average range.

### Calorie Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/calorie-calculator/

How many calories should you eat a day? Enter your age, sex, height, weight and activity level to get your maintenance calories, plus daily targets to lose or gain ½, 1 or 2 pounds a week. Charts below show typical needs by age and how many calories common activities burn.

Q: How many calories do I need a day?
A: Most adults need about 1,600 to 3,000 calories a day. Your exact number is your BMR (from the Mifflin-St Jeor equation) times an activity factor of 1.2 to 1.9. Eat about 500 fewer a day to lose roughly a pound a week.

Formula:
```
Men:    BMR = 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5
Women:  BMR = 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age − 161
TDEE   = BMR × activity factor
```

Example: A 34-year-old woman, 5 ft 6 in and 150 lb, has a BMR of about 1,397 kcal. With light exercise (factor 1.375) her maintenance is about 1,920 kcal a day.

### Calorie Deficit Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/calorie-deficit-calculator/

Find out how many calories to eat each day to lose weight, and roughly when you'll hit your goal. The calculator works out your maintenance calories, then subtracts a deficit for the pace you choose.

Q: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
A: Eat about 500 calories a day below your maintenance calories (TDEE) to lose roughly 1 lb a week. Don't go below 1,200 calories a day for women or 1,500 for men without medical supervision.

Formula:
```
TDEE = BMR (Mifflin-St Jeor) × activity factor
Daily deficit = pounds per week × 3,500 ÷ 7
Target calories = TDEE − deficit
```

Example: A 35-year-old woman, 5 ft 5 in and 180 lb, who exercises lightly has a TDEE of about 2,080 calories. To lose 1 lb a week she'd eat about 1,580 calories a day. Losing 20 lb at that pace takes about 20 weeks.

### Due Date Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/due-date-calculator/

Estimate a baby's due date from the first day of your last period, the conception date or an IVF transfer date, and see how far along you are and when each trimester ends.

Q: How do you calculate a due date?
A: Add 280 days (40 weeks) to the first day of your last menstrual period. Naegele's rule gives the same answer: add one year, subtract three months and add seven days. Only about 4% of babies arrive on the exact date.

Formula:
```
From last period:  due date = first day of period + 280 days (+ cycle length − 28)
From conception:  due date = conception + 266 days
IVF day-5 transfer:  due date = transfer + 261 days
```

Example: If the first day of your last period was January 1, 2026 and your cycle is 28 days, the estimated due date is October 8, 2026. The first trimester ends on April 8, 2026 and the second on July 15, 2026.

### Height Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/height-calculator/

How tall will your child be? Enter the mother's and father's heights to predict a boy's or girl's adult height with the mid-parental method doctors use, or use the toddler doubling rule.

Q: How tall will my child be?
A: The mid-parental height method averages the parents' heights and adjusts for sex: add 13 cm (5 inches) to the mother's height for a boy, or subtract 13 cm from the father's height for a girl, then average with the other parent.

Formula:
```
Boy = (father + mother + 13 cm) ÷ 2
Girl = (father + mother − 13 cm) ÷ 2
In inches: use 5 in instead of 13 cm
Likely range: ± 10 cm (about 4 in)
```

Example: Father 5 ft 10 in (70 in), mother 5 ft 5 in (65 in). A son is predicted at (70 + 65 + 5) ÷ 2 = 70 in (5 ft 10 in), likely between 5 ft 6 in and 6 ft 2 in. A daughter: (70 + 65 − 5) ÷ 2 = 65 in (5 ft 5 in).

### Ideal Weight Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/ideal-weight-calculator/

Find a healthy target weight for your height. The calculator gives your ideal body weight from four medical formulas and the weight range that puts you in the healthy BMI band of 18.5 to 24.9.

Q: How much should I weigh for my height?
A: For most adults, a healthy weight gives a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9. The Devine formula gives a single ideal weight: men 50 kg + 2.3 kg per inch over 5 ft, women 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg per inch.

Formula:
```
Devine (men) = 50 kg + 2.3 kg per inch over 5 ft
Devine (women) = 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg per inch over 5 ft
Healthy BMI weight = 18.5 to 24.9 × height (m)²
```

Example: A man who is 5 ft 10 in has 10 inches over 5 feet. Devine: 50 + 2.3 × 10 = 73 kg (161 lb). Robinson gives 71 kg (157 lb), Miller 70.3 kg (155 lb) and Hamwi 75 kg (165 lb). His healthy BMI range is 129–174 lb.

### Macro Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/macro-calculator/

Split your daily calorie target into grams of carbohydrate, protein and fat. Pick a balanced, high-protein, low-carb or keto split, or enter your own percentages.

Q: How do you calculate macros?
A: Each macronutrient has a fixed energy value: protein and carbohydrate have 4 calories per gram and fat has 9. The calculator takes the share of calories for each macro and divides by its calories per gram.

Formula:
```
Carbs (g) = calories × carb% ÷ 4
Protein (g) = calories × protein% ÷ 4
Fat (g) = calories × fat% ÷ 9
```

Example: On 2,200 calories a day with a balanced 50/20/30 split you'd eat 2,200 × 0.50 ÷ 4 = 275 g of carbs, 2,200 × 0.20 ÷ 4 = 110 g of protein and 2,200 × 0.30 ÷ 9 ≈ 73 g of fat.

### One Rep Max Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/one-rep-max-calculator/

Estimate the most weight you could lift for a single rep (your one rep max, or 1RM) from a set you've already done, without having to test a true max. Works for bench press, squat, deadlift and other lifts.

Q: How do you calculate your one-rep max?
A: The Epley formula estimates it as weight × (1 + reps ÷ 30). Lifting 200 lb for 5 reps gives about 233 lb. Estimates are most accurate from sets of 10 reps or fewer.

Formula:
```
Epley:    1RM = w × (1 + reps ÷ 30)
Brzycki:  1RM = w × 36 ÷ (37 − reps)
Lombardi: 1RM = w × reps^0.10
```

Example: Bench pressing 225 lb for 5 reps gives an Epley estimate of 225 × (1 + 5/30) = 262.5 lb. Brzycki gives 253.1 lb and Lombardi 264.3 lb. For sets of 8, about 80% of the Epley estimate, or roughly 210 lb, is a sensible working weight.

### Pace Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/pace-calculator/

Enter how far you ran and how long it took to get your pace per mile and per kilometre, your speed, and the finish time for a 5K, 10K, half marathon and marathon at the same pace.

Q: How do you calculate running pace?
A: Divide your time by the distance. A 5K in 27:30 is 27.5 ÷ 3.107 = 8.85 minutes per mile, or about 8:51 per mile (5:30 per km).

Formula:
```
Pace = time ÷ distance
Speed = distance ÷ time
1 mile = 1.609344 km
```

Example: A 5K (3.107 miles) in 28:00 is a pace of 9:01 per mile or 5:36 per km, a speed of about 6.66 mph (10.7 km/h). Held for a full marathon, that pace finishes in about 3:56:18.

### Period & Ovulation Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/period-calculator/

Enter the first day of your last period and your usual cycle length to predict your next period, your ovulation day and your most fertile days, for the next six months.

Q: How do you calculate your next period?
A: Add your cycle length to the first day of your last period. With a 28-day cycle that started on November 1, your next period is due around November 29, and ovulation is about 14 days before that.

Formula:
```
Next period = last period start + cycle length
Ovulation ≈ next period − 14 days
Fertile window = ovulation − 5 days to ovulation + 1 day
```

Example: Your last period started on November 1 and your cycle is 28 days. Your next period is due on November 29. Ovulation is around November 15, and your fertile window runs from November 10 to November 16.

### Protein Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/protein-calculator/

Work out how many grams of protein to eat each day based on your weight and goal, from the minimum for general health to the higher amounts used for building muscle or keeping it while losing fat.

Q: How much protein do I need a day?
A: The RDA is 0.8 g per kg of body weight (about 0.36 g per pound), roughly 55 g for a 150 lb adult. People who lift weights or want to keep muscle while losing weight often aim for 1.2–2.0 g per kg.

Formula:
```
Protein (g/day) = weight (kg) × grams per kg
weight (kg) = weight (lb) × 0.4536
```

Example: A 180 lb (81.6 kg) person lifting weights to build muscle needs about 1.6–2.2 g per kg, which is 131–180 g of protein a day, or roughly 33–45 g at each of four meals. The RDA minimum for the same person is 65 g.

### Sleep Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/sleep-calculator/

Find bedtimes and wake-up times that line up with 90-minute sleep cycles, so you are more likely to wake at the end of a cycle than in the middle of deep sleep.

Q: What time should I go to bed?
A: Count back from your wake-up time in 90-minute sleep cycles and add about 15 minutes to fall asleep. To wake at 6:00 AM after five cycles (7.5 hours), go to bed around 10:15 PM. Most adults need at least 7 hours.

Formula:
```
Bedtime  = wake-up time − cycles × 90 min − time to fall asleep
Wake time = bedtime + time to fall asleep + cycles × 90 min
```

Example: To wake at 6:30 AM, taking 15 minutes to fall asleep, go to bed at 10:45 PM for five cycles or 9:15 PM for six.

### TDEE Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/tdee-calculator/

Your TDEE (total daily energy expenditure) is how many calories you burn in a day, including exercise. Eat that many to keep your weight steady, fewer to lose weight, or more to gain. Enter your details and activity level to get yours.

Q: What is TDEE and how is it calculated?
A: TDEE (total daily energy expenditure) is the calories you burn in a day. It's your BMR from the Mifflin-St Jeor equation multiplied by an activity factor: 1.2 for desk work up to 1.9 for very hard training.

Formula:
```
BMR (men) = 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5
BMR (women) = 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age − 161
TDEE = BMR × activity factor
```

Example: A 30-year-old man, 5 ft 10 in (178 cm) and 180 lb (81.6 kg), who exercises 3–5 days a week: BMR = 1,783 calories. TDEE = 1,783 × 1.55 = 2,763 calories a day. To lose about a pound a week he'd aim for around 2,263.

### Water Intake Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/water-intake-calculator/

Estimate how much water to drink each day based on your body weight and how much you exercise. Results are shown in ounces, cups and litres, alongside the official adequate intake for adults.

Q: How much water should I drink a day?
A: A common rule of thumb is to drink half an ounce of water for every pound you weigh (about 33 ml per kg), then add about 12 ounces (350 ml) for every 30 minutes of exercise.

Formula:
```
Base (oz) = weight (lb) × 0.5
Exercise: + 12 oz per 30 minutes
Hot weather: + 16 oz
1 cup = 8 oz   1 litre = 33.8 oz
```

Example: A 160 lb person who exercises for 30 minutes a day needs about 160 × 0.5 + 12 = 92 ounces, which is 11.5 cups or 2.7 litres a day.

## Money

### Auto Loan Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/auto-loan-calculator/

Estimate your monthly car payment with the vehicle price, down payment, trade-in, sales tax and loan term all included.

Q: How do you calculate a car payment?
A: Work out the amount financed: price minus down payment and trade-in, plus sales tax and fees. Then apply the loan formula: payment = amount × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n), with r the monthly rate and n the number of months.

Formula:
```
Amount financed = price − down payment − trade-in + sales tax + fees
Monthly payment = A × r(1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1)
```

Example: A $34,000 car with $4,000 down, a $3,000 trade-in and 7% sales tax ($2,170) leaves $29,170 to finance. At 6.9% for 60 months the payment is $576.23. Over 48 months it is $697.16 with $4,294 interest; over 72 months it is $495.92 with $6,536 interest.

### CD Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/cd-calculator/

See how much a certificate of deposit (CD) will earn. Enter the deposit, the APY and the term to get the interest earned and the balance at maturity, plus the same deposit over other common terms.

Q: How do you calculate CD interest?
A: Banks quote CD rates as an annual percentage yield (APY), which already includes the effect of compounding. That makes the maths simple: the balance grows by the APY each year, so after t years it is deposit × (1 + APY)ᵗ, whether the bank compounds daily or monthly.

Formula:
```
Balance = deposit × (1 + APY)^(months ÷ 12)
Interest = balance − deposit
```

Example: $10,000 in a 1-year CD at 4.50% APY earns $450. In an 18-month CD at the same APY it earns about $682.54.

### Compound Interest Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/compound-interest-calculator/

See how a starting amount and regular monthly deposits grow with compound interest, with a year-by-year table of deposits, interest and balance.

Q: How do you calculate compound interest?
A: Use A = P × (1 + r/n)^(n × t), where P is the starting amount, r the annual rate as a decimal, n the compounding periods per year and t the years. $10,000 at 5% compounded yearly for 10 years grows to $16,289.

Formula:
```
Without deposits:  A = P × (1 + r/k)^(k×t)
P = starting amount, r = yearly rate, k = compounding periods per year, t = years
```

Example: $10,000 at 7% compounded monthly, plus $200 a month for 10 years, grows to about $54,714. You put in $34,000, so about $20,714 is interest.

### Discount Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/discount-calculator/

Enter the original price and the percent off to see the sale price and how much you save. Add an extra discount for stacked deals like “25% off plus an extra 10%”, and sales tax for the total at the register.

Q: How do you calculate a discount?
A: The sale price is the original price multiplied by (1 − discount ÷ 100). A $80 item at 25% off costs $80 × 0.75 = $60, so you save $20.

Formula:
```
Sale price = price × (1 − discount ÷ 100)
Stacked: price × (1 − d1 ÷ 100) × (1 − d2 ÷ 100)
You save = price − sale price
```

Example: A jacket tagged $80 is 25% off, with an extra 10% off at checkout. First discount: $80 × 0.75 = $60. Extra discount: $60 × 0.90 = $54. You save $26, which is 32.5% off.

### Gas Cost Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/gas-cost-calculator/

Estimate how much gas a road trip will cost. Enter the distance, your car's fuel economy and the price per gallon, choose one way or round trip, and split the cost between passengers.

Q: How do you calculate gas cost for a trip?
A: Fuel used is the distance divided by your miles per gallon. Multiply that by the price per gallon to get the cost.

Formula:
```
Gallons = miles ÷ MPG
Cost = gallons × price per gallon
Metric: litres = km × L/100 km ÷ 100
```

Example: A 300-mile trip in a car that gets 28 MPG, with gas at $3.10 a gallon: 300 ÷ 28 = 10.7 gallons × $3.10 = $33.21 one way, or $66.43 for the round trip. Split between 3 people, that's $22.14 each.

### House Affordability Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/house-affordability-calculator/

Find a realistic home price for your budget. Enter your income, monthly debts, down payment and mortgage rate, and the calculator applies the debt-to-income rules lenders use, including property tax, insurance, HOA fees and PMI.

Q: How much house can I afford?
A: Under the 28/36 rule, total housing costs should be no more than 28% of gross monthly income, and all debts no more than 36%. On a $100,000 salary that's about $2,333 a month, or roughly a $320,000 home with $40,000 down at 6.5%.

Formula:
```
Max housing payment = lower of
  28% × monthly income
  36% × monthly income − other debts
Home price = down payment + loan the payment supports
(after property tax, insurance, HOA and PMI)
```

Example: A household earning $100,000 a year with $500 of monthly debts and $40,000 down, at a 6.5% 30-year rate: 28% of $8,333 is $2,333 and 36% minus debts is $2,500, so the limit is $2,333 a month. After taxes, insurance and PMI that supports a home of about $320,000.

### Loan Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/loan-calculator/

Work out the monthly payment on a personal loan, debt consolidation loan or any fixed-rate loan. Enter the amount, APR and term to get the payment, the total interest, a year-by-year schedule, and how much you'd save by paying extra.

Q: How do you calculate a loan payment?
A: Use payment = P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n), where P is the amount borrowed, r the monthly rate (APR ÷ 12) and n the number of months. A $20,000 loan at 9.5% APR for 5 years costs about $420 a month.

Formula:
```
Payment = P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n)
r = APR ÷ 12 ÷ 100,  n = number of monthly payments
Total interest = payment × n − P
```

Example: A $20,000 loan at 9.5% APR over 5 years (60 payments) costs $420.04 a month. You'd pay $5,202 in interest, $25,202 in total.

### Margin Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/margin-calculator/

Enter your cost and selling price to see the profit, gross margin and markup. Or enter the cost and the margin (or markup) you want, and get the price to charge.

Q: How do you calculate profit margin?
A: Gross margin = (price − cost) ÷ price × 100. Selling for $60 something that cost $40 is a 33.3% margin. Markup uses cost instead: (price − cost) ÷ cost × 100 = 50%.

Formula:
```
Profit = price − cost
Margin = profit ÷ price × 100
Markup = profit ÷ cost × 100
Price for a target margin = cost ÷ (1 − margin)
```

Example: A product costs $40 and you want a 30% margin. Price = 40 ÷ (1 − 0.30) = $57.14. Profit is $17.14, which is a 42.9% markup.

### Mortgage & Loan Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/mortgage-calculator/

Find the monthly payment for a mortgage or any fixed-rate loan, with optional property tax, home insurance, PMI, HOA fees and extra payments. See the payoff date, the interest you'll pay and a yearly or monthly amortization schedule.

Q: How do you calculate a monthly mortgage payment?
A: Use the amortization formula: payment = P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n), where P is the loan amount, r the monthly rate (annual rate ÷ 12) and n the number of payments. Then add property tax, insurance and any HOA or PMI for the full monthly cost.

Formula:
```
M = P × r(1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1)
P = loan amount   r = yearly rate ÷ 12   n = number of monthly payments
```

Example: A $350,000 loan at 6.5% over 30 years costs $2,212.24 a month. Over 360 payments you pay $796,406, of which $446,406 is interest. The same loan over 15 years costs $3,048.88 a month but only $198,798 in interest.

### Percentage Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/percentage-calculator/

Three percentage calculators in one: find X% of a number, what percent one number is of another, and the percentage change between two values.

Q: How do you calculate a percentage of a number?
A: Multiply the number by the percentage and divide by 100. 20% of 150 is 150 × 20 ÷ 100 = 30. To find what percent X is of Y, divide X by Y and multiply by 100.

Formula:
```
X% of Y          = X ÷ 100 × Y
X as % of Y      = X ÷ Y × 100
Percent change   = (new − old) ÷ |old| × 100
```

Example: 15% of 240 is 36. 45 is 25% of 180. A price that moves from 80 to 100 has risen by +25%.

### RMD Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/rmd-calculator/

Work out how much you must withdraw from a traditional IRA, 401(k) or 403(b) this year. Enter your birth year and last year's December 31 balance to get your RMD, using the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table, and a 10-year projection.

Q: How do you calculate your RMD?
A: Your RMD is last year's December 31 balance divided by the distribution period for your age at the end of this year, from the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table.

Formula:
```
RMD = balance on Dec 31 of the prior year ÷ distribution period
Distribution period: IRS Uniform Lifetime Table, by age at year end
```

Example: You were born in 1952, so you turn 74 in 2026. Your IRA held $500,000 on December 31, 2025. The factor for age 74 is 25.5, so your 2026 RMD is 500,000 ÷ 25.5 = $19,608, due by December 31, 2026.

### Sales Tax Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/sales-tax-calculator/

Add sales tax to a price, or remove it from a total to find the price before tax. Works for US sales tax, UK and Dutch VAT, Canadian GST and HST, and Australian GST.

Q: How do you calculate sales tax?
A: To add tax, multiply the price by the rate and add it on. To remove tax from a total, divide by 1 plus the rate.

Formula:
```
Total = price × (1 + rate)
Price before tax = total ÷ (1 + rate)
Tax = total − price before tax
```

Example: A $100 item with 7% sales tax costs $107. Going the other way, a £120 total with 20% VAT has a price before tax of £100 and £20 of VAT.

### Save Our Homes Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/save-our-homes-calculator/

Florida's Save Our Homes cap limits how much the assessed value of a homestead can rise each year, to 3% or the inflation rate, whichever is lower. Enter the year you got your homestead exemption, its value then and its market value now to see your capped assessed value, how much tax the cap saves you, and how much benefit you could carry to a new home.

Q: How does Florida's Save Our Homes cap work?
A: When you first qualify for a homestead exemption, your assessed value equals the market value. From the next January 1, the assessed value can rise by no more than 3% or the change in the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower, and never above market value.

Formula:
```
Assessed(year) = min(market value, assessed(last year) × (1 + cap))
cap = lower of 3% or CPI change (2.7% for 2026)
Save Our Homes benefit = market value − assessed value
Tax = (assessed − exemptions) × millage ÷ 1,000
```

Example: A home that got its homestead exemption in 2015 at a value of $250,000 and is worth $450,000 in 2026 has a capped assessed value of about $320,336, so $129,664 of value isn't taxed. At 6 school mills and 11.5 other mills, the 2026 tax is about $4,865 instead of $7,134: a saving of $2,269 this year and about $12,928 since 2015.

### Simple Interest Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/simple-interest-calculator/

Work out simple interest on a loan or savings with the formula I = P × r × t. Enter the principal, annual rate and time to get the interest, the total amount, and how it compares with compound interest.

Q: How do you calculate simple interest?
A: Use I = P × r × t: principal times the annual rate as a decimal times the time in years. $10,000 at 5% for 3 years earns 10,000 × 0.05 × 3 = $1,500 in interest.

Formula:
```
I = P × r × t
Total (A) = P × (1 + r × t)
r = annual rate ÷ 100,  t = years
```

Example: $10,000 at 5% for 3 years: I = 10,000 × 0.05 × 3 = $1,500. The total is $11,500. Compounded yearly, the same deposit would earn $1,576.25.

### Tip Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/tip-calculator/

A free tip calculator: enter the bill, pick a tip percentage, and see the tip amount, the total and what each person pays when you split the bill.

Q: How do you calculate a tip?
A: The tip is the bill multiplied by the tip percentage. Add it to the bill and divide by the number of people to get each share.

Formula:
```
Tip = bill × tip % ÷ 100
Each person = (bill + tip) ÷ people
```

Example: A $86.40 bill with an 18% tip is $15.55 in tip and $101.95 in total. Split three ways, each person pays $33.98.

## Math

### Average Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/average-calculator/

Paste or type a list of numbers to find the average (mean), median, mode, range, sum, count and geometric mean, with the working shown. Below you'll also find how to do a weighted average, average percentages, and the Excel and Google Sheets formulas.

Q: How do you calculate the average?
A: Add all the numbers and divide by how many there are. The average of 4, 8 and 15 is (4 + 8 + 15) ÷ 3 = 9. The median is the middle value when the numbers are sorted.

Formula:
```
Mean = sum ÷ count
Median = middle value of the sorted list
Mode = most frequent value
Range = largest − smallest
```

Example: For 4, 8, 15, 16, 23 and 42, the sum is 108 and there are 6 numbers, so the mean is 108 ÷ 6 = 18. The median is the mean of 15 and 16, which is 15.5. No number repeats, so there is no mode. The range is 42 − 4 = 38.

### Fraction Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/fraction-calculator/

Add, subtract, multiply or divide two fractions or mixed numbers. The answer is simplified and shown as a fraction, a mixed number, a decimal and a percent, with the working.

Q: How do you add fractions with different denominators?
A: To add or subtract, the fractions need a common denominator. The calculator uses the least common multiple of the two denominators, rewrites both fractions over it, then adds or subtracts the tops.

Formula:
```
a/b + c/d = (a×d + c×b) ÷ (b×d)
a/b × c/d = (a×c) ÷ (b×d)
a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c
```

Example: 3/4 + 5/6: the common denominator is 12, so it becomes 9/12 + 10/12 = 19/12, which is 1 7/12 or 1.583333.

### Long Division Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/long-division-calculator/

Enter a dividend and divisor to get the quotient and remainder, with every long-division step written out. Great for checking homework: you also get the decimal answer and the mixed number.

Q: How do you do long division?
A: Long division breaks a big division into small ones, working left to right through the digits of the dividend. At each step you divide the current number by the divisor, write the whole-number result in the quotient, multiply it back, subtract, and bring down the next digit.

Formula:
```
Dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder
0 ≤ remainder < divisor
```

Example: 1,764 ÷ 13: 17 ÷ 13 = 1, remainder 4. Bring down 6: 46 ÷ 13 = 3, remainder 7. Bring down 4: 74 ÷ 13 = 5, remainder 9. The answer is 135 R 9, or 135 9/13 ≈ 135.692. Check: 13 × 135 + 9 = 1,764.

### Percent Change Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/percent-change-calculator/

Work out the percentage change between an old value and a new one, for prices, salaries, grades, sales or stock prices. You can also increase or decrease a number by a percentage, and see what it takes to get back to the start.

Q: How do you calculate percent change?
A: Subtract the old value from the new value, divide by the old value and multiply by 100. From 80 to 100 is (100 − 80) ÷ 80 × 100 = 25%; a negative result is a percentage decrease.

Formula:
```
Percent change = (new − old) ÷ |old| × 100
Increase by p% = value × (1 + p ÷ 100)
Decrease by p% = value × (1 − p ÷ 100)
```

Example: A stock goes from $80 to $100: (100 − 80) ÷ 80 × 100 = +25%. If it then falls back to $80, that's (80 − 100) ÷ 100 × 100 = −20%, not −25%.

### Quadratic Formula Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/quadratic-formula-calculator/

Solve a quadratic equation in the form ax² + bx + c = 0. Enter a, b and c to get both roots (real or complex), the discriminant, the vertex of the parabola and the working.

Q: How do you solve a quadratic equation?
A: For ax² + bx + c = 0, use x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a. If b² − 4ac is positive there are two real roots, if it's zero there's one, and if it's negative the roots are complex.

Formula:
```
x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a
Discriminant D = b² − 4ac
Vertex: x = −b ÷ 2a
```

Example: For x² − 5x + 6 = 0, a = 1, b = −5 and c = 6. The discriminant is 25 − 24 = 1, so x = (5 ± 1) ÷ 2, giving x = 3 and x = 2. The factored form is (x − 3)(x − 2) = 0.For 2x² + 4x − 6 = 0 the discriminant is 16 + 48 = 64, and the roots are x = 1 and x = −3.

### Ratio Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/ratio-calculator/

Find the missing number in a proportion such as 3:4 = 12:?, and simplify any ratio to its lowest terms. Useful for scaling recipes, mixing concrete or paint, map scales, screen sizes and homework.

Q: How do you solve a ratio or proportion?
A: Two ratios are in proportion when they are equal fractions: A/B = C/D. Cross-multiplying gives A × D = B × C, so the missing value is D = B × C ÷ A.

Formula:
```
A : B = C : D   →   D = B × C ÷ A
Simplify: divide A and B by GCF(A, B)
```

Example: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour to 4 cups of milk. With 12 cups of flour you need 4 × 12 ÷ 3 = 16 cups of milk. The ratio 18:24 simplifies to 3:4, which is also 1:1.333.

### Right Triangle Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/right-triangle-calculator/

Enter any two sides of a right triangle to find the third side with the Pythagorean theorem, both acute angles, the area and the perimeter. Leave the side you want to find blank.

Q: How do you find the hypotenuse of a right triangle?
A: Use the Pythagorean theorem: c = √(a² + b²). With legs of 3 and 4, the hypotenuse is √(9 + 16) = 5. To find a missing leg, use a = √(c² − b²).

Formula:
```
a² + b² = c²
c = √(a² + b²)     a = √(c² − b²)
A = sin⁻¹(a ÷ c)   B = 90° − A
Area = a × b ÷ 2
```

Example: Legs of 5 and 12 give a hypotenuse of √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13. The angles are about 22.62° and 67.38°, the area is 30 and the perimeter is 30.

### Rounding Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/rounding-calculator/

Round a number to the nearest whole number, ten, hundred, tenth, hundredth or thousandth, and see it rounded to every place at once. You can also pick the rounding rule: half up, banker's rounding, always up, always down or truncate.

Q: How do you round a number?
A: To round, look at the digit just to the right of the place you're rounding to. If it's 5 or more, round up; if it's 4 or less, keep the digit and drop the rest.

Formula:
```
Look at the next digit to the right:
0–4 → round down (keep the digit)
5–9 → round up (add 1 to the digit)
```

Example: 2,746.385 rounds to 2,746.39 (hundredths), 2,746.4 (tenths), 2,746 (whole number), 2,750 (tens) and 2,700 (hundreds). With banker's rounding, 2,746.385 to the hundredth still gives 2,746.38, because 8 is even.

### Scientific Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/scientific-calculator/

A free online calculator for everyday sums and scientific maths: trigonometry in degrees or radians, logarithms, powers, roots, percentages and factorials. Type on your keyboard or tap the keys.

Q: What order should you do operations in?
A: The calculator follows the standard order of operations: brackets first, then powers and roots, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction.

Formula:
```
Order of operations: ( )  →  ^ √ !  →  × ÷  →  + −
x% = x ÷ 100        EXP: 3E5 = 3 × 10⁵
log = base 10        ln = base e (2.71828…)
```

Example: sin(30) in degrees is 0.5. 2^10 is 1024, √(144) is 12, 5! is 120 and log(1000) is 3. To find 15% of 80, type 80 × 15% to get 12.

### Slope Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/slope-calculator/

Enter two points to find the slope of the line through them, the equation in slope-intercept form (y = mx + b), the y-intercept, the angle of the line, the distance between the points and the midpoint.

Q: How do you find the slope of a line?
A: Slope = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁): the change in y divided by the change in x between two points. For (1, 2) and (4, 8), the slope is (8 − 2) ÷ (4 − 1) = 2.

Formula:
```
m = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁)
b = y₁ − m × x₁        y = mx + b
d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²)
angle = tan⁻¹(m)
```

Example: For the points (2, 3) and (6, 11), the slope is (11 − 3) ÷ (6 − 2) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2. The intercept is 3 − 2 × 2 = −1, so the line is y = 2x − 1. The points are √(4² + 8²) ≈ 8.944 apart and the line rises at about 63.43°.

### Standard Deviation Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/standard-deviation-calculator/

Paste or type a list of numbers to get the sample and population standard deviation, the variance, mean, median, range and count.

Q: How do you calculate standard deviation?
A: Find the mean, subtract it from each value and square the results. Add the squares, divide by n − 1 for a sample (or n for a whole population), and take the square root.

Formula:
```
Mean  x̄ = Σx ÷ n
Population SD  σ = √( Σ(x − x̄)² ÷ n )
Sample SD  s = √( Σ(x − x̄)² ÷ (n − 1) )
```

Example: For 10, 12, 23, 23, 16, 23, 21, 16 the mean is 18 and the squared differences add up to 192. The population standard deviation is √(192 ÷ 8) = 4.899 and the sample standard deviation is √(192 ÷ 7) = 5.237.

### Z-Score Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/z-score-calculator/

Enter a raw score, the mean and the standard deviation to get the z-score, plus the percentile and probabilities from the normal distribution. No z-table needed.

Q: How do you calculate a z-score?
A: z = (x − μ) ÷ σ: subtract the mean from the value and divide by the standard deviation. A score of 85 on a test with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 10 has z = 1.5, about the 93rd percentile.

Formula:
```
z = (x − μ) ÷ σ
Percentile = Φ(z) × 100
Two-tailed p = 2 × (1 − Φ(|z|))
```

Example: A test has a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 10. A score of 85 has z = (85 − 70) ÷ 10 = 1.5. That's higher than about 93.32% of test takers (the 93rd percentile).

## Home

### Concrete Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/concrete-calculator/

Work out how much concrete you need for a slab, patio, path or post holes, in cubic yards, cubic feet or cubic metres, and how many bags to buy.

Q: How do you calculate how much concrete you need?
A: Multiply length × width × thickness in feet to get cubic feet, then divide by 27 for cubic yards. A 10 × 10 ft slab 4 inches thick needs 10 × 10 × 0.333 ÷ 27 = 1.23 cubic yards. Add about 10% for waste.

Formula:
```
Slab (cu ft)   = length (ft) × width (ft) × thickness (in) ÷ 12
Cubic yards    = cubic feet ÷ 27
Post hole      = π × (diameter ÷ 2)² × depth
Bags           = volume ÷ bag yield, rounded up
```

Example: A 10 × 10 ft patio, 4 inches thick, needs 33.33 cubic feet, or 1.23 cubic yards. With 10% extra that is 1.36 cubic yards, or 62 bags of 80 lb premix. Eight fence post holes, each 10 inches wide and 36 inches deep, need 14.4 cubic feet with 10% extra, which is 24 bags of 80 lb concrete.

### Gravel Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/gravel-calculator/

Work out how much gravel, crushed stone or sand to order for a driveway, path or patio. Enter the area and depth, pick the material, and get the amount in cubic yards, tons and bags.

Q: How do you calculate how much gravel you need?
A: Multiply length × width in feet by depth in inches, divide by 12 for cubic feet and by 27 for cubic yards. Multiply cubic yards by about 1.4 to get tons. A 40 × 12 ft driveway 4 in deep needs about 5.9 cubic yards, or 8.3 tons.

Formula:
```
Cubic yards = length (ft) × width (ft) × depth (in) ÷ 12 ÷ 27
Tons = cubic yards × density (≈ 1.4 for gravel)
Cubic metres = length (m) × width (m) × depth (cm) ÷ 100
```

Example: A 40 × 12 ft driveway, 4 inches deep: 40 × 12 × 4 ÷ 12 = 160 cubic feet, ÷ 27 = 5.93 cubic yards. At 1.4 tons per yard that's about 8.3 tons of gravel.

### Mulch Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/mulch-calculator/

Work out how much mulch, topsoil or gravel you need for a garden bed. Enter the size and depth to get cubic feet, cubic yards and the number of bags to buy.

Q: How do you calculate how much mulch you need?
A: Multiply the bed's length × width in feet by the depth in inches, divide by 12 for cubic feet, then by 27 for cubic yards. A 10 × 20 ft bed 3 inches deep needs about 1.85 cubic yards.

Formula:
```
Volume (ft³) = length × width × depth (in) ÷ 12
Circle: 3.1416 × radius² × depth ÷ 12
Cubic yards = ft³ ÷ 27
```

Example: A 20 ft × 10 ft bed at 3 inches deep needs 20 × 10 × 3 ÷ 12 = 50 cubic feet, which is 1.85 cubic yards, or 25 two-cubic-foot bags (17 three-cubic-foot bags).

### Paint Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/paint-calculator/

Find out how much paint a room needs in gallons or litres, allowing for doors, windows, the ceiling and the number of coats.

Q: How do you calculate how much paint you need?
A: Multiply the room's perimeter by the wall height, subtract about 20 sq ft per door and 15 per window, multiply by the number of coats, and divide by the coverage on the can, usually about 350–400 sq ft per gallon.

Formula:
```
Wall area   = 2 × (length + width) × height − doors − windows
Paint       = (wall area + ceiling) × coats ÷ coverage
```

Example: A 14 × 12 ft bedroom with 8 ft walls, one door and two windows has about 366 sq ft of wall. Two coats at 350 sq ft per gallon need 2.09 gallons, so buy 2 gallons and a quart, or 3 gallons. In metric, a 4.2 × 3.6 m room with 2.4 m walls has about 32.7 m² of wall and needs about 6.5 litres for two coats.

### Square Footage Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/square-footage-calculator/

Measure the area of rooms and shapes in square feet or square metres, add a waste allowance and estimate material cost for flooring, tile, carpet or turf.

Q: How do you calculate square feet?
A: Multiply the length by the width in feet. A 12 × 15 ft room is 180 square feet. For a circle use π × radius², for a triangle ½ × base × height, and add up the pieces of an L-shaped room.

Formula:
```
Rectangle = length × width
Circle    = π × (diameter ÷ 2)²
Triangle  = base × height ÷ 2
1 m² = 10.764 sq ft     1 sq yd = 9 sq ft
```

Example: A 14 × 12 ft room is 168 sq ft (15.6 m²). With 10% waste you need 184.8 sq ft, and at $4.50 per sq ft the flooring costs about $831.60.

### Stair Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/stair-calculator/

Plan stairs for a deck, basement or loft. Enter the total rise from floor to floor and your tread depth, and the calculator works out how many steps you need, the exact riser height, the total run and the stringer length.

Q: How do you calculate stairs?
A: Divide the total rise by the maximum riser height (7¾ in under US residential code) and round up to get the number of risers. Divide the rise by that number for each riser's height. Treads = risers − 1, and total run = treads × tread depth.

Formula:
```
Risers = ⌈total rise ÷ max riser⌉
Riser height = total rise ÷ risers
Treads = risers − 1
Total run = treads × tread depth
Stringer ≈ √(rise² + run²)
```

Example: A basement with a 108-inch rise (9 ft): 108 ÷ 7.75 = 13.9, so 14 risers of 108 ÷ 14 = 7.71 in. That gives 13 treads; at 10.5 in each, the total run is 136.5 in (11 ft 4.5 in). The stringer is about 174 in long.

### Tile Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/tile-calculator/

Work out how many tiles you need for a floor, wall, shower or backsplash. Enter the area, your tile size and grout gap, and the calculator adds a waste allowance and tells you how many boxes to buy.

Q: How do you calculate how many tiles you need?
A: Divide the area to cover by the area of one tile, then add 10% for cuts and breakage (15% for diagonal layouts). A 120 sq ft floor with 12 × 24 in tiles (2 sq ft each) needs 60 tiles, or 66 with waste.

Formula:
```
Tile area = (length + grout) × (width + grout)
Tiles = room area ÷ tile area × (1 + waste ÷ 100)
Boxes = tiles ÷ tiles per box, rounded up
```

Example: A 12 × 10 ft floor (120 sq ft) with 12 × 24 in tiles: each tile covers 2 sq ft, so you need 60 tiles. With 10% waste that's 66 tiles, or 9 boxes of 8. With 1/8-inch grout joints each tile covers slightly more floor, so the calculator shows 65.

### Turkey Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/turkey-calculator/

Plan your Thanksgiving or Christmas turkey. Enter the number of guests or the turkey's weight and your dinner time to see how big a bird to buy, when to start thawing it, how long to roast it, and when it needs to go in the oven.

Q: How long do you cook a turkey?
A: At 325°F, an unstuffed turkey takes roughly 13 to 16 minutes per pound: about 3 to 3¾ hours for 12–14 lb and 3¾ to 4¼ hours for 14–18 lb. It's done when the thickest part of the breast, thigh and wing reaches 165°F.

Formula:
```
Size: guests × 1–1.5 lb
Fridge thaw: 1 day per 4–5 lb
Cold-water thaw: 30 min per lb
Done at 165°F (74°C) · rest 20–30 min
```

Example: For 12 guests with leftovers, buy a turkey of about 12 × 1.5 = 18 lb. Thawing it in the fridge takes 4 to 5 days, so for Thursday dinner put it in the fridge by Saturday or Sunday. Unstuffed, an 18 lb turkey roasts for about 4¼ to 4½ hours at 325°F, so for dinner at 5:00 PM it goes in the oven at about 12:00 PM.

## Students

### Character Counter
URL: https://numbrik.com/character-counter/

Type or paste text to count characters with and without spaces, letters and words. Bars show how much room you have left for X posts, text messages, Instagram captions, YouTube titles and Google titles and descriptions.

Q: Do spaces count as characters?
A: Yes. Letters, numbers, spaces, punctuation and line breaks all count as characters, and limits like X's 280 or an SMS's 160 include spaces. The “without spaces” count leaves out spaces, tabs and line breaks.

Formula:
```
Characters = every letter, digit, space and symbol
Without spaces = characters − spaces, tabs and line breaks
```

Example: “Hello, world!” has 13 characters, 12 without the space, 10 letters and 2 words.

### Final Grade Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/final-grade-calculator/

Find out what score you need on your final exam to reach the grade you want, whether that's keeping an A or making sure you pass.

Q: What do I need on my final exam?
A: Required score = (target grade − current grade × (1 − final weight)) ÷ final weight. With an 85% average, a final worth 25% and a 90% target, you need (90 − 85 × 0.75) ÷ 0.25 = 105%, so a 90 isn't reachable.

Formula:
```
Needed on final = (target − current × (1 − final weight)) ÷ final weight
```

Example: With a current grade of 84% and a final worth 25%, you need 88% on the final to finish with 85%. To get a 90% (an A), you would need 108%, which isn't possible without extra credit.

### GCF Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/gcf-calculator/

Find the greatest common factor (GCF) of 2 to 20 whole numbers. It's also called the greatest common divisor (GCD) or highest common factor (HCF). Each number's prime factorization is shown so you can check the answer.

Q: How do you find the greatest common factor?
A: The greatest common factor is the largest number that divides every number in the list without a remainder. With prime factorization, multiply the primes the numbers share, each at its lowest power.

Formula:
```
GCF(a, b) = GCF(b, a mod b), until the remainder is 0
```

Example: 48 = 2⁴ × 3, 180 = 2² × 3² × 5 and 72 = 2³ × 3². The shared primes at their lowest powers are 2² × 3 = 12. With Euclid: 180 mod 48 = 36, 48 mod 36 = 12, 36 mod 12 = 0, so GCF(180, 48) = 12.

### GPA Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/gpa-calculator/

Add your courses, letter grades and credits to get your semester GPA on the 4.0 scale. Add your current GPA and credits to see your new cumulative GPA.

Q: How do you calculate GPA?
A: Each letter grade has a grade-point value. The calculator multiplies each grade's points by the course credits, adds them up and divides by the total credits, so a 4-credit course counts more than a 1-credit lab.

Formula:
```
GPA = Σ(grade points × credits) ÷ Σ credits
Cumulative = (current GPA × earned credits + new grade points) ÷ (earned + new credits)
```

Example: The example term has five courses worth 14 credits and 50.4 grade points, a semester GPA of 3.60. A student who already had a 3.40 GPA over 45 credits would move to a cumulative 3.45.

### Grade Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/grade-calculator/

Work out your current grade in a class from weighted assignments and categories, such as homework, quizzes, exams and projects. See your percentage and letter grade straight away.

Q: How do you calculate a weighted grade?
A: Most classes give each category a weight, such as homework 20% and exams 50%. Your grade is a weighted average: each score is multiplied by its weight, the results are added up, and the total is divided by the sum of the weights.

Formula:
```
Grade = Σ(score × weight) ÷ Σ weight
Score % = points earned ÷ points possible × 100
```

Example: The example class has homework at 92% (weight 20), quizzes at 85% (15), a midterm at 78% (25), a project at 88% (15) and participation at 100% (5). That adds up to 6,885 weighted points over 80 weight, a current grade of 86.1%, which is a B. The final exam, worth the remaining 20%, is still to come.

### LCM Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/lcm-calculator/

Find the least common multiple of 2 to 20 whole numbers, with the prime factorization of each number shown.

Q: How do you find the least common multiple?
A: The least common multiple is the smallest positive number that every number in your list divides into evenly. One way to find it is prime factorization: write each number as a product of primes and multiply together the highest power of every prime that appears.

Formula:
```
LCM(a, b) = a × b ÷ GCF(a, b)
LCM(a, b, c) = LCM(LCM(a, b), c)
```

Example: 12 = 2² × 3, 18 = 2 × 3² and 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. Taking the highest power of each prime gives 2² × 3² × 5 = 180.

### Word Counter
URL: https://numbrik.com/word-counter/

Paste or type your text to count words, characters, sentences and paragraphs instantly. You also get the reading time, speaking time and most-used keywords, which helps with essays, blog posts, speeches and word limits.

Q: How do you count the words in a text?
A: Paste the text into a word counter: every run of letters or numbers between spaces counts as one word, so “don't” and “2026” are one word each. At an average reading speed of 238 words a minute, 1,000 words takes about 4 minutes to read.

Formula:
```
Reading time = words ÷ 238 per minute
Speaking time = words ÷ 140 per minute
Average word length = letters ÷ words
```

Example: A 1,500-word blog post takes about 6 minutes 18 seconds to read (1,500 ÷ 238) and about 10 minutes 43 seconds to read aloud (1,500 ÷ 140).

## Dates & time

### Age Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/age-calculator/

Find your exact age in years, months and days, your age in total days and weeks, and how long until your next birthday.

Q: How do you calculate your exact age?
A: Subtract your birth year from the current year, then take off one if your birthday hasn't happened yet this year. For the exact age, count the full months since your last birthday and then the remaining days.

Formula:
```
Age = full years + full months + remaining days between the two dates
```

Example: Someone born on March 17, 1994 is 32 years, 7 months and 3 days old on October 20, 2026. That is 11,905 days, or about 1,700 weeks.

### Date Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/date-calculator/

Add days, weeks, months or years to a date, or subtract them, and get the exact date and day of the week. Use it for deadlines, notice periods, contract dates, warranties and “90 days from” questions.

Q: How do you add days to a date?
A: Count forward that many calendar days from the start date, including weekends. 90 days after November 8, 2026 is February 6, 2027. Adding months keeps the same day of the month, or the last day if that date doesn't exist.

Formula:
```
Result = start date + years + months (calendar) + weeks × 7 + days
If the day doesn't exist in the new month, use the month's last day
```

Example: From November 8, 2026, adding 90 days gives Saturday, February 6, 2027. Adding 3 months instead gives Monday, February 8, 2027, because months have different lengths.

### Days Between Dates
URL: https://numbrik.com/days-between-dates/

Count the days, weeks and weekdays between two dates, or count down to a holiday, deadline or trip.

Q: How do you count the days between two dates?
A: Subtract the earlier date from the later one. By convention the start date isn't counted and the end date is, so Monday to Friday of the same week is 4 days. Add 1 if you want to include both dates.

Formula:
```
Days = end date − start date
Weeks = days ÷ 7
```

Example: From October 20, 2026 to Christmas Day is 66 days, which includes 48 weekdays and is about 9.4 weeks.

### Half Birthday Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/half-birthday-calculator/

Your half birthday is the day exactly six months after your birthday. Enter your date of birth to see when your next half birthday is, how many days are left, and how old you'll be (and a half).

Q: When is my half birthday?
A: The calculator adds six calendar months to your birthday. Someone born on March 10 has a half birthday on September 10.

Formula:
```
Half birthday = birthday + 6 calendar months
If that day doesn't exist, use the last day of the month
```

Example: Born on March 10, your half birthday is September 10. Born on August 31, your half birthday is February 28 (February 29 in a leap year such as 2028).

### Military Time Converter
URL: https://numbrik.com/military-time-converter/

Convert military time (the 24-hour clock) to standard 12-hour time with AM and PM, or the other way round. Type a time in either box, or use the 24-hour chart below.

Q: How do you convert military time to standard time?
A: For hours 13 to 23, subtract 12 and add PM: 1730 is 5:30 PM. 0000 is 12:00 AM (midnight), 1200 is noon, and hours 01 to 11 are the same in the morning, so 0845 is 8:45 AM.

Formula:
```
PM hours (1–11 PM):  military = hour + 12
Military 1300–2359:   standard = hour − 12, PM
12:00 AM = 0000      12:00 PM = 1200
```

Example: 6:30 PM is 6 + 12 = 18, so it's 1830. Military 0545 is 5:45 AM, and 2215 is 22 − 12 = 10:15 PM.

### Time Zone Converter
URL: https://numbrik.com/time-zone-converter/

Convert a time from one time zone to another, for meetings, calls, flights and live events. Pick a date and time, choose the two zones, and get the converted time, the difference, and the time in eight major cities.

Q: How do you convert between time zones?
A: Find each zone's offset from UTC on that date and add the difference. Eastern Standard Time is UTC−5 and India is UTC+5:30, so India is 10½ hours ahead: 9:00 AM EST is 7:30 PM IST.

Formula:
```
UTC time = local time − zone offset
Target time = UTC time + target offset
Example offsets: EST = UTC−5, PST = UTC−8, IST = UTC+5:30
```

Example: A call at 9:00 AM Pacific on Monday, November 9, 2026 is 12:00 PM Eastern, 5:00 PM in London and 10:30 PM in India. In summer, while the US is on daylight time, the same 9:00 AM PDT call would be 9:30 PM in India.

### Working Days in a Year
URL: https://numbrik.com/working-days-calculator/

Count the working days in any year or month. There are 261 weekdays in 2026, and 250 working days after the 11 US federal holidays. Choose a year and add your own vacation days to see the days you'll actually work.

Q: How many working days are in a year?
A: Most years have 260 or 261 weekdays. Take off the 11 US federal holidays that fall on weekdays and a typical US year has about 250 working days, or roughly 2,000 working hours.

Formula:
```
Working days = weekdays − weekday holidays − PTO days
Work hours = working days × 8
```

Example: 2026 has 261 weekdays. All 11 federal holidays fall on or are observed on a weekday, leaving 250 working days, or 2,000 hours at 8 hours a day. With 15 days of vacation you'd work 235 days. In 2027, New Year's Day 2028 falls on a Saturday and is observed on Friday, December 31, 2027, so 2027 has 249 working days.

## Work & pay

### Hourly to Salary Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/hourly-to-salary-calculator/

Convert an hourly wage into yearly, monthly, biweekly and weekly pay, or work backwards from a salary to an hourly rate.

Q: How do you convert an hourly wage to a yearly salary?
A: Multiply the hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. A full-time US year is 40 × 52 = 2,080 hours, so $25 an hour is about $52,000 a year before tax. Divide a salary by 2,080 to go the other way.

Formula:
```
Annual pay  = hourly rate × hours per week × paid weeks
Hourly rate = annual pay ÷ (hours per week × paid weeks)
```

Example: $25 an hour at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks is $52,000 a year, $4,333.33 a month and $2,000 every two weeks, before tax.

### Hours Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/hours-calculator/

Find how many hours are between two times. Enter a start and end time, such as 8 AM and 5 PM, and the hours calculator shows the total in hours and minutes, decimal hours and minutes, minus any unpaid break. It handles overnight shifts like 7 PM to 7 AM, counts hours between two dates, and adds hours to a time. The charts below answer the most common shifts at a glance.

Q: How do you calculate hours between two times?
A: Convert both times to minutes after midnight, subtract the start from the end, and take off any break. If the end time is earlier than the start, the period crosses midnight, so add 24 hours. Divide the minutes by 60 for decimal hours.

Formula:
```
Minutes = end − start − break   (add 1,440 if end is before start)
Decimal hours = minutes ÷ 60
```

Example: From 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM is 9 hours (540 minutes, 9.00 decimal hours). Take off a 30-minute unpaid lunch and the time worked is 8 hours 30 minutes, or 8.50 decimal hours. Overnight, 7:00 PM to 7:00 AM is 12 hours.

### Pay Raise Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/pay-raise-calculator/

See your new pay after a raise. Enter your current hourly wage or salary and the raise as a percentage or an amount, or enter your old and new pay to find the raise percentage.

Q: How do you calculate a pay raise?
A: A percentage raise multiplies your pay by one plus the percentage: a 4% raise on $50,000 is $50,000 × 1.04 = $52,000.

Formula:
```
New pay = old pay × (1 + raise% ÷ 100)
Raise % = (new pay − old pay) ÷ old pay × 100
Yearly = hourly × 2,080
```

Example: A 5% raise on $24.00 an hour gives $25.20 an hour, which is $52,416 a year, or $2,496 more than before. Going from $50,000 to $53,000 is a raise of 3,000 ÷ 50,000 = 6%.

### Take-Home Pay Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/take-home-pay-calculator/

Estimate your take-home pay per paycheck in the United States for 2026, after federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare, an estimated state tax and pre-tax deductions such as a 401(k).

Q: How do you calculate take-home pay?
A: Start with gross pay, subtract pre-tax deductions such as 401(k) contributions, then subtract federal income tax, Social Security (6.2%), Medicare (1.45%) and any state income tax. What's left is your net pay.

Formula:
```
Taxable income = salary − pre-tax deductions − standard deduction
Federal tax    = sum of each bracket slice × its rate
Social Security = 6.2% × min(salary, $184,500)
Medicare       = 1.45% × salary (+0.9% above $200,000 single / $250,000 joint)
Take-home      = salary − pre-tax − federal − Social Security − Medicare − state
```

Example: A single filer earning $65,000 with no pre-tax deductions in a state with no income tax pays about $5,620 in federal income tax, $4,030 in Social Security and $942 in Medicare. Take-home pay is about $54,408 a year, or $2,092.60 every two weeks. A married couple earning $100,000 together, putting $6,000 into a 401(k) and paying an estimated 5% state tax, takes home about $74,730 a year.

### Time Card Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/time-card-calculator/

Enter start and end times for each day, take off unpaid breaks, and get total hours, overtime and gross pay for the week. Overtime rules follow the region you pick at the top of the page.

Q: How do you calculate hours on a time card?
A: For each day, subtract the clock-in time from the clock-out time, then subtract unpaid breaks. Add the days together for the weekly total. Under the US federal rule, hours over 40 in a workweek are overtime, paid at 1.5 times the regular rate.

Formula:
```
Daily hours   = (end − start − break minutes) ÷ 60
Overtime      = max(0, weekly hours − threshold)
Gross pay     = regular hours × rate + overtime × rate × multiplier
```

Example: The calculator opens with an example week: five weekday shifts and a short Saturday, totalling 43.25 hours. At $22.50 an hour with overtime after 40 hours at 1.5×, that is 40 regular hours ($900.00) plus 3.25 overtime hours at $33.75 ($109.69), for gross pay of $1,009.69.

### Time to Decimal Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/time-to-decimal-calculator/

Convert time in hours and minutes to decimal hours for payroll, invoices and timesheets, or turn decimal hours back into hours and minutes. A chart of every minute from 1 to 59 is below.

Q: How do you convert minutes to decimal hours?
A: Divide the minutes by 60 and add them to the hours. 7 hours 45 minutes is 7 + 45 ÷ 60 = 7.75 hours. To go back, multiply the decimal part by 60: 0.3 hours is 18 minutes.

Formula:
```
Decimal hours = hours + minutes ÷ 60 + seconds ÷ 3,600
Minutes = (decimal hours − whole hours) × 60
```

Example: A shift of 8 hours 20 minutes is 8 + 20 ÷ 60 = 8.33 hours (8.333…). At $22 an hour that's 8.333 × $22 = $183.33.

## Fun

### Coin Flip
URL: https://numbrik.com/coin-flip/

Flip a virtual coin for a quick heads-or-tails decision, or flip it up to 1,000 times and see the totals and the longest streak.

Q: Is an online coin flip 50/50?
A: Each flip takes one random value from your browser's cryptographic generator and turns it into heads or tails, so both sides have exactly a 50% chance and earlier flips never affect the next one.

Formula:
```
Chance of heads = 1 ÷ 2
Chance of k heads in a row = (1 ÷ 2)ᵏ
```

Example: The chance of three heads in a row is ½ × ½ × ½ = 12.5%. Ten heads in a row is 1 in 1,024, or about 0.1%.

### Dice Roller
URL: https://numbrik.com/dice-roller/

Roll virtual dice for board games, tabletop role-playing games and classroom games. Choose d4 to d100, roll up to 50 dice at once and add a modifier.

Q: Is an online dice roller truly random?
A: A good one is. This roller uses your browser's cryptographic random number generator, so every face has an equal chance and no roll can be predicted from earlier rolls.

Formula:
```
Chance of one face on a die = 1 ÷ number of sides
Range of NdS + M = (N + M) to (N × S + M)
```

Example: 2d6 + 3 can land anywhere from 5 to 15. A single d20 gives each number, including a natural 20, a 5% chance.

### Life Path Number Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/life-path-number-calculator/

Find your life path number, the best-known number in numerology, from your date of birth. Add your full birth name to get your expression (destiny) and soul urge numbers too. It's just for fun.

Q: How do you calculate your life path number?
A: In Pythagorean numerology, your life path number comes from your birth date. Reduce the month, the day and the year separately to a single digit by adding their digits, then add the three results and reduce again.

Formula:
```
Reduce month, day and year to one digit each
Life path = reduce(month + day + year)
Keep 11, 22 and 33 as master numbers
```

Example: Born July 23, 1990: month 7 → 7; day 23 → 2 + 3 = 5; year 1990 → 1 + 9 + 9 + 0 = 19 → 1 + 9 = 10 → 1. Then 7 + 5 + 1 = 13 → 1 + 3 = 4.

### Love Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/love-calculator/

Type your name and your crush's name to get a love percentage. It's a party game, not science, but the same two names always get the same score, so you can't just keep pressing until you win.

Q: How does a love calculator work?
A: The score comes from the letters of both names, sorted so it doesn't matter whose name goes first. The letters are fed through a hash, a formula that scrambles text into a number, and the number is turned into a percentage between 35% and 100%.

Formula:
```
score = 35 + (hash(sorted names) mod 66)
Same two names → same score, in either order
```

Example: Type Alex and Sam and you'll always get the same score, whether Alex or Sam goes first. Try “Alexander” instead and the score changes.

### Password Generator
URL: https://numbrik.com/password-generator/

Create strong, random passwords with your chosen length and character types. Passwords are made in your browser and are never sent anywhere.

Q: What makes a strong password?
A: Length matters most: use at least 14–16 random characters, mixing upper and lower case, numbers and symbols, and never reuse a password. A random generator and a password manager are the easiest way to do this.

Formula:
```
Entropy (bits) = length × log₂(number of possible characters)
```

Example: A 16-character password using uppercase, lowercase, numbers and 24 symbols draws from 86 characters, giving about 103 bits of entropy. That rates as very strong.

### Random Number Generator
URL: https://numbrik.com/random-number-generator/

Pick one random number or up to 1,000 in any range, with or without repeats. Use it for raffles, games, classroom draws or choosing a winner.

Q: How do you pick a random number?
A: Numbers come from your browser's cryptographic random number generator. The calculator also uses rejection sampling, which throws away the few raw values that would make some numbers slightly more likely, so every number in the range has exactly the same chance.

Formula:
```
Chance of a given number = 1 ÷ (highest − lowest + 1)
Ways to draw k of n without repeats = n! ÷ (k! × (n − k)!)
```

Example: Picking one number from 1 to 100 gives each number a 1% chance. Drawing 6 numbers from 1 to 49 with no repeats can produce 13,983,816 different sets, so the chance of matching all six is 1 in 13,983,816.

## Converters

### Bra Size Calculator
URL: https://numbrik.com/bra-size-calculator/

Measure your underbust and bust with a soft tape, enter the numbers, and get your bra size in US, UK and EU sizing, plus sister sizes to try if the first doesn't fit perfectly.

Q: How do you measure your bra size?
A: Your band size is your underbust measurement rounded to the nearest even number of inches. Your cup size is the difference between your bust and your band: each inch is one cup size, so 1 inch is an A, 2 inches a B, 3 a C, 4 a D and 5 a DD.

Formula:
```
Band = underbust (in), rounded to the nearest even number
Cup = bust − band (1 in = A, 2 = B, 3 = C, 4 = D, 5 = DD…)
EU band = 70 + (US band − 32) ÷ 2 × 5
```

Example: Underbust 31.5 in rounds to a 32 band. Bust 36 in: 36 − 32 = 4 inches = D cup. Your size is 32D (UK 32D, EU 70D). Sister sizes: 30DD and 34C.

### Roman Numeral Converter
URL: https://numbrik.com/roman-numeral-converter/

Type a number to get it in Roman numerals, or type Roman numerals to get the number. It also converts years and full dates, which is handy for tattoos, clock faces, film credits and Super Bowl numbers.

Q: How do you convert numbers to Roman numerals?
A: Break the number into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones and write each with I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500 and M = 1,000, using IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM for 4s and 9s. 2026 = MM + XX + VI = MMXXVI.

Formula:
```
I = 1   V = 5   X = 10   L = 50
C = 100   D = 500   M = 1000
IV = 4  IX = 9  XL = 40  XC = 90  CD = 400  CM = 900
```

Example: To write 2026: 2000 = MM, 20 = XX, 6 = VI, so 2026 = MMXXVI. To read MCMXCIV: M (1000) + CM (900) + XC (90) + IV (4) = 1994.

### Shoe Size Converter
URL: https://numbrik.com/shoe-size-converter/

Convert a shoe size between US, UK and European (EU) sizing for men, women and kids, or measure your foot and find your size in every system. Full conversion charts are below.

Q: How do you convert US shoe sizes to EU?
A: Measure foot length in inches: US men = 3 × inches − 22 and EU = 1.27 × (UK size + 23) + 2. By that formula a men's US 9 is about EU 41.5, a US 10 about EU 42.5 and a women's US 8 about EU 39; brands vary by half a size.

Formula:
```
US men = 3 × foot (in) − 22
US women = 3 × foot (in) − 21
UK = 3 × foot (in) − 23
EU = 1.27 × (UK + 23) + 2
foot (in) = foot (cm) ÷ 2.54
```

Example: A men's US 10 fits a foot of about 10.67 inches (27.1 cm). That's a UK 9, an EU 42.5 and a women's US 11. A women's US 8 is a UK 6 and an EU 39.

### Unit Converter
URL: https://numbrik.com/unit-converter/

Convert kitchen measures, length, weight and temperature, including US cups, metric cups, tablespoons, feet, metres, pounds, kilograms, °F, °C and kelvin.

Q: How do you convert between metric and US units?
A: Multiply by a conversion factor: 1 inch = 2.54 cm, 1 mile = 1.609 km, 1 pound = 0.4536 kg, 1 US gallon = 3.785 litres. For temperature, °F = °C × 9/5 + 32.

Formula:
```
°C = (°F − 32) × 5 ÷ 9
°F = °C × 9 ÷ 5 + 32
K  = °C + 273.15
```

Example: 1.5 US cups is 354.9 ml. An oven at 350°F is 176.7°C, which recipes usually round to 180°C (gas mark 4).
